answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is non-negotiable and the incumbent has refused to reopen pricing, eliminating both renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms as viable paths this cycle. memory_c2 records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — I am verifying that record because the entire decision rests on whether that prior performance is reliable under the tighter timeline (14 days) and the no-buffer assembly condition. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the 18% mandate alone, so no second-source spend is required, which also satisfies the 'exactly one sourcing decision' constraint. memory_c3's lesson (dual-sourcing removes single-point-of-failure risk) is noted as a follow-up for the next review cycle rather than this one, because it would consume the single decision slot without addressing the immediate cost mandate. The 94% line utilization with no buffer is the primary delivery-risk factor; mitigating it relies on the verified onboarding speed from memory_c2 and the option to hold the incumbent on month-to-month terms (memory_c5 precedent) during the transition window.
